note.question: How should randomized robust price be optimized?
note.overview: The robust multiproduct pricing problem is to determine the prices of a collection of products to maximize the worst-case revenue, where the worst case is taken over an uncertainty set of demand models that the firm expects could be realized in practice. A tacit assumption in this approach is that the pricing decision is a deterministic decision: the prices of the products are fixed and do not vary. In this paper, we consider a randomized approach to robust pricing, where a decision maker specifies a distribution over potential price vectors to maximize its worst-case revenue over an uncertainty set of demand models.
